acceptance_criteria: A downstream lane can receive previous lane output by ContextBundle or artifact ref.
Message payload artifact refs are replayable after process restart.
ContextBundle records selected, rejected, and unresolved lane outputs.

When a ModelLaneMessage carries a CRDT proposal for shared editable state, the payload artifact MUST include schema_id, document_id, workspace_id, actor_id, actor_kind, lane_id, crdt_site_id, update_seq, Yjs-compatible update_bytes_ref, update_sha256, state_vector, base_snapshot_ref, materialized_projection_hash, replay_metadata, and PromotionGate/ValidationRunner refs. CRDT payloads are pre-promotion evidence only until validated and promoted through EventLedger authority.

ContextBundle handoff entries MUST be typed records, not opaque prompt text: source_lane_id, source_message_id, artifact_ref, artifact_sha256/content_hash, source_kind, authority_state, selection_state selected|rejected|unresolved|superseded, reason_code, reviewer/decision_ref, created_at, and replay_hint. Downstream lanes MUST consume these records by id/ref, and tests MUST prove reconstruction without raw prompt replay.

When a ModelLaneMessage or ContextBundle references Loom-derived context or output, it MUST carry stable Loom refs: workspace_id, block_id, optional source_block_id/target_block_id, artifact_ref when materialized, content_hash/version, and EventLedger/Flight Recorder evidence.

FEMS use is bounded: MemoryPack entries are reviewable, scope-tagged, cloud-safe when sent to cloud lanes, and never treated as unverified authority over current EventLedger/CRDT state. Hidden provider/session memory MUST NOT substitute for MemoryPack.
CRDT handoff preserves state-vector/proposal metadata and requires semantic review/promotion for rich editable surfaces; mechanical merge is not acceptance.

ContextBundle handoff MUST add or extend embedded SurrealDB storage for model-lane handoff selection state with run_id, source_lane_id, source_message_id, artifact_ref, artifact_sha256, selection_state, reason_code, decision_ref, EventLedger event id, and replay query API.
Negative proof MUST fail closed when selected, rejected, unresolved, or superseded artifact refs are missing, hash-mismatched, or not replayable.

After implementation and before READY_FOR_VALIDATION, this MT MUST receive post-implementation adversarial review against the actual diff. Findings must be fixed or converted into explicit lifecycle blocker/missing_resource/proof_status state; the implementer may not self-certify COMPLETED.
scope.risk_if_missed: Cloud and local models cannot reliably speak across restart or validator review.

implementation_notes: Use ContextBundle and artifact refs as the only durable way one model lane gives another lane prior output.
Payload artifacts must live in ArtifactStore/EventLedger/embedded-SurrealDB-backed authority, not temp files or prompt-only memory.
ContextBundle must record selected, rejected, unresolved, and superseded lane outputs with reason metadata.
If shared editable state is touched by operator and model lanes, use CRDT draft/update semantics and promote through ValidationRunner/PromotionGate.
No raw prompt replay should be required to reconstruct a handoff; the project-named internal viewing tool must show enough artifact/message state for recovery.

LangGraph-style checkpoint/store separation maps to ContextBundle for run-local handoff and FEMS/Loom/UserManual for durable cross-run memory/knowledge, all under embedded-SurrealDB/EventLedger authority.
Peritext-style user-intent risk means rich text or work-surface CRDT merges need validation/preview/promotion records before becoming authority.
Payload refs should be large-data references with bounded summaries because EventLedger and Flight Recorder evidence refs should not carry unbounded model output bodies.

Use EventLedger payloads plus Flight Recorder evidence refs as bounded events/artifact refs; do not put unbounded model output, raw secrets, or prompt-only state in event payloads. Direct Flight Recorder event emission for this surface is deferred to MT-008 diagnostics.

If this MT changes any product behavior, storage/event contract, command, IPC/API path, diagnostic surface, model lane, or navigation path, update the in-product UserManual in the same implementation change per HBR-MAN-004.

Product implementation for this MT must be Rust-only: Rust backend plus Rust native egui/Argus surfaces where UI is touched. Legacy app/src, app/src-tauri, React, Tauri/WebView, TypeScript, JavaScript, docs/model-manual, and npm proof targets are reference-only or forbidden and MUST NOT satisfy implementation/proof authority.

Proof commands must name exact Rust test targets or exact test names. Zero matching tests is a hard failure. Deterministic provider fakes are allowed for cloud/local model calls, but embedded SurrealDB/EventLedger/ArtifactStore/CRDT/UserManual/Argus authority must touch real Handshake-owned Rust resources.
Each behavior-changing MT must include same-change UserManual coverage for the changed behavior; MT-011 audits coverage and cannot substitute for same-change HBR-MAN-004 proof.

This pre-implementation contract review does not replace post-implementation review. After coding, run adversarial review against the actual diff through the listed lenses and update MT status signaling before handoff.
